bihar_raw_news.title: UP CM directs officials to accelerate budget expenditure, financial sanctions - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 UP CM directs officials to accelerate budget expenditure, financial sanctions Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday directed officials to speed up the issuance of financial sanctions and ensure faster utilisation of funds allocated under the 2026-27 state budget. Reviewing the budget provisions and expenditure of major departments, Adityanath said the first half of the financial year was nearing its end and called for immediate corrective measures wherever utilisation was below expectations. The chief minister directed departments to issue 70 per cent of financial sanctions within the next two months and ensure expenditure of at least 60 per cent of their allocated budgets, the state government said. The meeting, attended by Finance Minister Suresh Khanna, reviewed the financial and operational progress of 30 major departments that account for the largest budget allocations. Adityanath said the objective of the budget was not merely to allocate funds but to ensure their timely utilisation and delivery of benefits to people. He directed the finance minister to hold regular, point-by-point reviews of expenditure with departmental ministers. Departments facing policy, procedural or technical hurdles in securing approvals or spending funds should be provided immediate solutions, he said, directing the Finance Department to monitor the progress and regularly update the Chief Minister's Office. The chief minister also stressed the need to improve the credit-deposit ratio of banks to strengthen the rural economy. He directed officials to ensure that every eligible farmer receives the benefits of the Kisan Credit Card scheme and ordered village-wise and farmer-wise mapping to identify eligible beneficiaries and link them with banking facilities. He also asked officials to prepare a framework for events such as the 'Rural Credit Conclave' to improve the availability of credit in rural areas and strengthen the banking system. On promoting local products, Adityanath directed the MSME Department to undertake branding and extensive promotion of Uttar Pradesh's GI-tagged products to expand their reach in domestic and international markets. He stressed that there should be no compromise on the quality or timely completion of public welfare schemes and development projects. In cases of unnecessary delays or substandard work, accountability should be fixed on the concerned agencies and responsible officials, the statement said. During a review of centrally assisted schemes, Adityanath directed departments to ensure better coordination for programmes dependent on funds from the Centre. He asked departmental ministers to communicate directly with their central counterparts to resolve issues related to pending funds and approvals so that implementation of centrally assisted schemes was not delayed. The chief minister also directed heads of departments and senior officials to undertake regular field visits to review development works and take immediate corrective action wherever progress was slow. He asked departments to meet their targets within the remaining months of the financial year. "There will be no shortage of funds for schemes related to development and public welfare. bihar_raw_news.title: India Launches AI-First Digital Tourism Stack To Simplify Travel Discovery And Booking
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / India Launches AI-First Digital Tourism Stack To Simplify Travel Discovery And Booking Launched on World Tourism Day 2026, the National Digital Tourism Stack will be its “list once, reach multiple platforms” model. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: September 28, 2026 1:38 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Pexels/Miriam Espacio The Ministry of Tourism and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) have launched the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS), an open digital infrastructure aimed at making India’s tourism ecosystem more accessible, discoverable and connected. Scroll down to know more. Ministry Of Tourism & ONDC Launches National Digital Tourism Stack Launched on World Tourism Day 2026 in the presence of Union Tourism and Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, the initiative will connect tourism businesses, destinations and travellers across participating digital platforms. The Stack is designed to help smaller tourism providers and lesser-known destinations gain access to a wider digital market. The initiative comes as India’s tourism sector continues to support millions of jobs and businesses across hospitality, transport, food, retail, handicrafts, homestays and local experiences. According to Ministry of Tourism data, the sector contributed 5.22 per cent to India’s GDP and supported 8.46 crore jobs in 2023-24. A key feature of the National Digital Tourism Stack will be its “list once, reach multiple platforms” model. Homestays, guides, attractions and experience providers will be able to list their offerings once and make them discoverable across participating applications, reducing the need to maintain separate digital integrations. For travellers, the platform aims to bring different parts of a journey together through shared digital infrastructure. This could include stays, experiences, transport, routes and last-mile mobility, reducing the need to use multiple platforms to plan and book a trip. Also Read: Cab Driver Argues Darjeeling Toy Train Was On ‘Wrong Side’ After Video Captures Collision Stack To Support Newer Ways Of Planning Travel The Stack is also being developed as an AI-first infrastructure. It is intended to support newer ways of discovering and planning travel, including AI-led interfaces and personal digital agents. The broader vision includes bringing different parts of a traveller’s journey together through concepts such as “One ticket, One pass”. The ecosystem is expected to cover more than 23,000 tourism experiences and homestays. More than 1,000 tourism experiences are already transacting on the ONDC Network, including 170 ASI monuments and 29 museums. Also Read: This Wood And Stone Cabin Near Darjeeling Can Be Booked At Just ₹1,028 Per Night Trust will also form a core part of the initiative, with features planned around provider credentials, service quality, ratings and reviews, payments, identity requirements and grievance redressal. The Ministry of Tourism will work with states and Union Territories to curate and validate tourism experiences. ONDC, meanwhile, will provide the open digital infrastructure connecting tourism providers and participating platforms. The initiative is intended to help bring more local businesses and lesser-known destinations into India’s growing digital tourism ecosystem. bihar_raw_news.title: CM lays foundation for 53 projects worth Rs 214 crore | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 28, 2026 CM lays foundation for 53 projects worth Rs 214 crore Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta laid foundation stones for 53 development projects worth Rs 214.12 crore in unauthorised colonies across Kirari, Bawana, Mundka, Narela and Nangloi Jat Assembly constituencies on Sunday. The projects are under the Seva Sankalp campaign, aimed at strengthening civic amenities for around 1.75 lakh residents. The Chief Minister said the Delhi government's objective is to strengthen basic civic amenities across the city, with development works now being undertaken in a planned manner in areas that have long faced infrastructure problems. She said roads, drains, sewerage and drainage are basic rights of every citizen, and the Government is ensuring development reaches every lane and area of Delhi. Under the 53 projects, 1,062 roads and lanes in 27 unauthorised colonies will be developed, along with around 89.82 km of road network and 147.69 km of drainage network, to improve local connectivity and reduce waterlogging. North West Delhi MP Yogendra Chandolia, Cabinet Ministers Parvesh Sahib Singh, Ashish Sood and Ravindra Indraj Singh, and MLAs Raj Karan, Manoj Shokeen and Gajendra Daral attended the event. Kirari Assembly constituency accounts for the largest share of the projects, with 27 development works to be undertaken in 14 unauthorised colonies at a cost of Rs 105.51 crore, including development of 640 roads and lanes, 50.71 km of roads and 101.42 km of drainage network. Bawana will see nine works worth Rs 38.83 crore, Mundka five works worth Rs 22.05 crore, Narela four works worth Rs 14.48 crore, and Nangloi Jat eight works worth Rs 33.25 crore. The stormwater drainage networks planned across these areas are expected to improve drainage and reduce waterlogging, while paved roads and lanes will improve connectivity and reduce dust from damaged surfaces. The Chief Minister said development work has gained new momentum following the change in government in Delhi after 27 years, with the Government focusing on permanent solutions to long-pending problems rather than merely making announcements. She said the government is working to fulfil basic needs across every lane, area and Assembly constituency, moving toward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resolve for a "Viksit Delhi," with emphasis on time-bound implementation on the ground. PWD and Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said the Government is committed to ensuring development reaches every lane and household in unauthorised colonies, not just main roads, describing the 53 projects as an important step toward resolving long-pending basic problems by strengthening road, sewerage and drainage infrastructure. Social Welfare Minister Ravindra Indraj Singh said adequate attention was not paid to development in the Kirari area during the previous Government's tenure, despite the Aam Aadmi Party remaining in power for a long period and continuing to hold the constituency's MLA seat. He said the Chief Minister had now made a budget of `105 crore available for the area, ensuring no discrimination in development works or budget allocation based on whether a constituency has an AAP

bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / Bihar Train Services Disrupted Due To Rajendra Pul Work; 35 Cancelled, 33 Diverted Several trains to and fro Bihar have been cancelled and diverted due to the ongoing NI work at Rajendra Pul. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: September 28, 2026 11:43 AM Share Indian Railways has cancelled 35 trains, diverted 33 others, and short-terminated or short-originated nine trains today due to non-interlocking (NI) work at Rajendra Pul in Bihar. Want to know more about it? Read on. Bihar Train Cancelled & Diverted Due To Work At Rajendra Pul According to reports by The Indian Express, the work is being carried out to commission a new rail bridge parallel to the existing Rajendra Bridge over the Ganga near Mokama. The new bridge will connect the existing railway network at Upper Hathidah Junction, Tal Junction, Rampur Dumra, Dinkar Gram Simaria and Barauni Junction. The 1.9-km rail-cum-road Rajendra Bridge connects Mokama and Barauni across the Ganga and has been operational since 1959. According to Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO) of East Central Railway (ECR), the existing bridge carries a single railway line and could not be doubled due to technical limitations. A parallel double-line bridge was subsequently approved in the 2015-16 Rail Budget at an estimated cost of ₹1,491.47 crore. bihar_raw_news.title: ITC Expands Dairy Business in East India With Value-Added Push - Siliconindia
bihar_raw_news.content: ITC Expands Dairy Business in East India With Value-Added Push By siliconindia | Monday, 28 September 2026, 10:50:19 AM IST ITC is strengthening its dairy presence in Eastern India by expanding its branded milk and value-added product portfolio. ITC is expanding its fresh dairy business in Eastern India, with a focus on branded milk and value-added products across Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand. The company sees growing potential as consumers increasingly move toward packaged dairy products with consistent quality. ITC entered the fresh dairy market in 2018 with Aashirvaad milk in Bihar and later expanded into West Bengal and Jharkhand. Its portfolio now includes fresh milk, curd, paneer, lassi and Mishti Doi. Hemant Malik , Chief Executive Officer, Foods Division, and Executive Director, ITC, said Eastern India will remain a key market for the company's dairy expansion. Malik told PTI, that, "East is one of the most promising growth markets for the dairy category and will be central to our growth strategy in the coming years". Bihar remains an important opportunity for the company, with more than 80 percent of consumers purchasing loose milk. ITC is targeting this market by expanding packaged milk and value-added products such as pouch curd. Malik says, " In South India, consumers moved to branded curd over a decade ago, and we wanted to enable a similar transition in Bihar. With our pouch curd offerings, we are helping consumers shift to branded curd that delivers assured quality and consistency, backed by the trust of ITC". Also Read: JPMorgan Eyes 2X Growth for GIFT City Business in Two Years The company is also evaluating newer and healthier dessert products as it looks to expand its value-added dairy portfolio beyond Mishti Doi. ITC operates dairy facilities across Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal and directly procures milk from farmers. Through Project Gomukh , it works with dairy farmers to improve milk productivity and quality while supporting their incomes. During FY26, the company supported around 33,300 dairy farmers across more than 560 villages in the three states through veterinary services, cattle feed and other animal husbandry initiatives. ITC said its Aashirvaad Svasti fresh dairy portfolio recorded strong growth in FY26, led by premium milk and value-added products such as curd, paneer, Mishti Doi and lassi. bihar_raw_news.title: Mohan Yadav swings pickaxe at own home as part of road-widening project - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 28, 2026 Mohan Yadav swings pickaxe at own home as part of road-widening project Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday personally wielded a pickaxe to begin the demolition of a portion of his ancestral house in Ujjain’s Abdalpura locality as part of a road-widening project being undertaken ahead of Simhastha 2028. Yadav, a native of Abdalpura, reached his ancestral house at around 10 am and performed a puja before formally launching the widening work. He then picked up a pickaxe and struck the structure himself, marking the beginning of the demolition. The road from Khajur Wali Masjid to Jiwajiganj police station in Ujjain’s old city area is being widened to 32 feet. As many as 272 houses lie along the stretch. Residents from different communities have voluntarily agreed to surrender portions of their properties for the project. The initiative is being seen as an example of public participation in the city’s infrastructure and beautification works ahead of Simhastha 2028. Local resident Kadar Bhai said widening the road would fulfil a long-standing demand, as the existing narrow stretch often made vehicular movement difficult. He said residents on both sides of the road had willingly agreed to provide space for the project. Pawan Panchal, who lives next to Yadav’s ancestral house, said the wider road would improve connectivity and benefit local businesses. He said better access could also increase the value of shops and residential properties in the area. Yadav’s sister, Kalawati Yadav, the presiding officer of the Ujjain Municipal Corporation, also owns a house on the same stretch, which falls within the widening corridor. Narendra Jain, who runs a milk shop in the locality, said the demolition of properties belonging to the chief minister and his family had sent a message that the development exercise applied equally to residents. He said people from different sections of society were participating in the Simhastha-related works. Former councillor Jagdish Panchal said the project would improve the area’s appearance and create better facilities for the large number of pilgrims and tourists expected to visit Ujjain during Simhastha. Abdalpura is among Ujjain’s oldest settlements, and the road connects Khajur Wali Masjid with Jiwajiganj police station. The widening is part of a broader infrastructure push to improve traffic movement and civic facilities across the city ahead of Simhastha 2028. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 NTPC, EDF sign pact to develop renewable energy projects in India Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service State-owned NTPC and EDF Power Solutions India have joined hands to jointly develop, own and operate pumped storage projects, hydropower projects, as well as other renewable energy (RE) projects and distribution business. This 50:50 JV shall undertake projects within India and neighbouring countries, NTPC said in a statement. The joint venture (JV) agreement was signed on September 25 in the presence of NTPC Chairman Gurdeep Singh and Bernard Fontana, Chairman and CEO of EDF SA, France. Through this strategic partnership, NTPC and EDF Power Solutions, a fully owned subsidiary of the French electricity company EDF (Électricité de France), are committed to establishing a responsible and innovative industrial company to develop, build and operate low-carbon power plants, as well as flexibility solutions and transmission assets. EDF and NTPC will leverage their respective expertise to provide tailor-made offers, drive the decarbonisation and global performance of electrical systems, aligned with India’s ambitious goals of 100 GW installed capacity of pumped storage projects by 2036. Considering their expertise and resources, both entities are poised to contribute significantly to India’s renewable energy market, driving innovation and fostering environmental stewardship. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Govt launches National Digital Tourism Stack with ONDC - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 Govt launches National Digital Tourism Stack to build digital public infrastructure for tourism Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Photo Credits: PTI The Centre on Sunday launched an initiative to build a national digital public infrastructure for tourism that will bring a wide range of travel products and services onto a shared digital ecosystem. The Ministry of Tourism has partnered with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to develop the National Digital Tourism Stack , which aims to onboard 23,000 tourism experiences and homestays and make them discoverable, trustable and bookable by the end of 2028, officials said. Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Shekhawat launched the project at Bharat Mandapam during an event marking World Tourism Day. The initiative, being developed with ONDC and supported by the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), is aimed at making India's tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy, the ministry said. The shared infrastructure will enable tourism providers to make their offerings available across participating platforms, with features including verified identities and supplier credentials, search and discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal. The programme will be implemented in phases in collaboration with the ministry, states, Union territories and the tourism industry. Tourism Secretary Bhuvnesh Kumar said artificial intelligence would form the front end of the project, with a vision of "One ticket, One pass" to bring different components of a tourist's journey together. "Currently, flights, hotels, cabs, boat rides, or even an 'aarti' at a temple, etc., need to be booked through different websites. This fragmentation makes the process a digitally painful experience for a tourist planning to visit places," Kumar said. The digital stack is intended to bring such services together through a unified digital ecosystem, he said. "The project has been approved, and we will start onboarding services. The ministry would be the catalyst and lead for this project. We will work with states and UTs to curate and validate experiences," Kumar said. A steering committee will be constituted for the initiative, Kumar said, inviting tourism stakeholders to participate. According to a flyer shared at the event, the onboarding target of 23,000 includes 14,000 tourism experiences and 9,000 homestays. Kumar said the initiative would also focus on tourism experiences that are not currently available online or have only a limited digital presence. The objective is to make travel to both major cities and smaller towns "easy, safe, and in one's preferred language", according to the project note. The digital public infrastructure is expected to help tourists discover more destinations, travel with greater confidence, book and pay conveniently and reduce paperwork. The preparation and development phase will run from October to December 2026, followed by a pilot phase from January to June 2027, during which the first batch of experiences and homestays will go live, Kumar said. The initiative will then be scaled up from July 2027 to December 2028 through a nationwide supply onboarding drive. The ministry also released the India Tourism Statistics

national_raw_news.content: India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes that demonstrated to the world a new example of the Narendra Modi government’s counter-terrorism policy. On September 28-29, 2016, the Indian Army carried out targeted surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads across the Line of Control (LoC) in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The operation was launched as a direct and decisive military response to the Uri terror attack earlier that month, in which 19 Indian soldiers lost their lives. The anniversary highlights a decade of evolving national security measures. The government noted that the resolve shown in 2016 laid the groundwork for subsequent bold actions, including the 2019 Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor in 2025. In his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani yesterday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the 2016 surgical strike against terrorist hideouts as a historic milestone. He said the surgical strike highlighted the role of the Indian Army in carrying out the operation across the LoC. PM Modi recalled how the world was astonished by the manner in which Indian soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terrorism. The Prime Minister said that India’s counter-terrorism approach has continued to evolve over the past decade, citing the Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor as examples. PM Modi said the surgical strike was India’s decisive response to the long-standing pain the country had endured due to terrorist attacks. The Prime Minister said India had suffered from terrorist attacks for a long time, recalling a period when serial blasts had become a frequent occurrence in the country. Referring to terrorist attacks in September 2008, Mr Modi recalled the serial blasts in Delhi on September 13, 2008, in which several innocent people lost their lives. The Prime Minister also recalled the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, which took place just weeks after the Delhi blasts. He said India’s approach to terrorism has changed and that the country now follows a “zero-tolerance policy against terrorism”.

national_raw_news.title: ECI revises timeline for Special Intensive Revision in Delhi 2 hours ago 67
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission of India has revised the schedule for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision 2026 in Delhi. According to the Chief Electoral Officer of Delhi, the last date to file claims and objections will be the 30th of next month. The notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue till the 30th of November. The final electoral roll will now be published on the 4th of December. The Delhi CEO further informed that special camps were successfully organised at all polling station locations in the NCT of Delhi yesterday for the enrolment of new voters through Form-6. Other electoral services were also provided during the camps. According to the statement, another round of special camps for the enrolment of young electors will be held at all colleges, universities and other educational institutions in the national capital on the 29th and 30th of this month. It stated that, as of today, over 2,98,400 hearings for notices issued in unmapped and logical discrepancy cases have been conducted in Delhi. The Commission reiterated its firm commitment to a transparent, participative and inclusive revision process, ensuring that no eligible citizen is left out while no ineligible person is included in the electoral roll.
